title: What We Can Save In A Time Of Endings | NOEMA
gist: Kat Hill walks the eroding Norfolk, Cumbria and Caithness coasts to argue that climate-driven endings force hard choices about what to defend, abandon or memorialise, drawing on Jonathan Lear's 'radical hope'. UK Shoreline Management Plans triage places, with nuclear sites fortified and marginal communities left to the sea.

themes.theme: Coastal triage under UK Shoreline Management Plans

insights.claim: UK Shoreline Management Plans decide coastal futures by weighing where to spend money on walls, with four options: do nothing, maintain, extend defenses, or realign assets.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Defense-versus-retreat policy determines which coastal assets keep public funding.
insights.locator: In the U.K., the Shoreline Management Plans

insights.claim: Sizewell B in Suffolk was extended from decommissioning by 2035 to 2055, and Sizewell C is being built on a 7-meter platform, though critics say that is not high enough and sea-level modelling stops at 2140 without covering long-lived nuclear waste.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Coastal nuclear sites carry long-tail flood-design risk that outlasts current planning horizons.
insights.locator: There are nuclear power plants in vulnerable places

insights.claim: Sellafield's legacy waste silos and ponds, including a leaking Magnox Swarf Silo, are being shored up against sea rise because toxic waste that never becomes safe and cannot be moved has to be fortified in place.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Nuclear legacy liabilities create unavoidable, rising defense spending on the Cumbrian coast.
insights.quote: Toxic waste that never becomes safe and cannot be moved will have to be fortified.

insights.claim: Protecting critical infrastructure creates losers: Braystones Beach huts below Sellafield are left undefended, with the Cumbria Coastal Strategy citing no economic justification for significant investment.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Cost-benefit rules systematically sacrifice marginal communities, creating local political friction.
insights.quote: there is no economic justification to providing significant investment at the present time.

insights.claim: Walls trade off against ecology and neighbours: sea walls destroy marshland, floodgates designed for receding high water do not suit permanent rise, and defenses block sand movement that protects nearby places.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Hard defenses push costs onto adjacent areas, raising the odds of later litigation and spending.
insights.quote: If we build sea walls, we destroy marshland. If we protect nuclear waste, we condemn coastal communities.
insights.locator: Moreover, walls and floodgates were designed

themes.theme: Managed retreat, property value and insurance

insights.claim: Fairbourne in Wales was publicly labeled for abandonment in 2019, after which house prices plummeted overnight, investment dried up, and trust in managed retreat was destroyed.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Official retreat designation alone can crash property values before any physical loss.

insights.claim: Insurers often no longer cover homes in at-risk coastal places, since insurance is a bet on the future.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Withdrawal of cover is a leading indicator of stranded coastal property value.
insights.quote: Insurance policies, which after all are a bet on the future

insights.claim: Residents resist retreat, building their own boulder and gravel embankments, because home gives meaning and stability.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Expect political resistance and ad hoc private defenses to complicate retreat policy.
insights.locator: The inhabitants are determined to stay

insights.claim: The National Trust has admitted it cannot contain threats to coastal sites and aims to work with the grain of nature.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Heritage owners are shifting from conservation to managed decline.

insights.claim: Heritage protection is selective: Castle Sinclair Girnigoe has received stabilisation funds while nearby Castle Bucholie, though listed, lacks resources and faces its fate.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Listing does not equal funding; resources follow profile.
insights.locator: Castle Sinclair Girnigoe, an impressive northern fortress

insights.claim: Preservation by listing cannot hold back time, and 'managed ruination' can write an 'anticipatory history' of absence, per Caitlin DeSilvey.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Conservation strategies may pivot toward documentation rather than physical preservation.
insights.quote: Preservation suggests we can protect things in the future by putting them on lists, but that’s not really true.
insights.locator: "Old" ruins were once homes or lives

insights.claim: Jonathan Lear's 'ontological vulnerability' describes the risk that a whole world of meaning collapses, and climate change may not kill everyone but may destroy what makes life meaningful.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Frames climate loss as cultural and meaning loss, which shapes adaptation politics.
insights.quote: Climate change may not kill everyone, but it may destroy the things that give life meaning.
insights.locator: This is what Jonathan Lear called ontological vulnerability

insights.claim: Archaeologists have recorded oral histories around Happisburgh and 3D-scanned its church so it survives in digital form, and Tuvalu aims to become the first 'digital nation'.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Digital preservation and statehood for sinking places is an emerging policy and tech niche.

insights.claim: The author concludes the response to endings is courage, care and selective salvage, embracing the world even as it disappears.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Narrative of adaptation over denial underpins public acceptance of retreat.
insights.quote: reach out and embrace the world even as it disappears.
insights.locator: There may not be a world of pure hope

themes.theme: Nature squeezed by sea level rise

insights.claim: Salt incursion into Norfolk's Broads, mudflats and marshes kills the invertebrates nesting waders feed on and washes away habitat, while 'sacrifice zone' language is spreading in environmental-justice debates.
insights.speaker: KAT HILL
insights.so_what: Habitat loss adds an ecological dimension to coastal defense permitting and trade-offs.
